### Helper models

Models this attack drives, configured under its `roles`. Each one is a [ModelConfig](../../cli/campaign-files/target.md#modelconfig).

| Role | Kind | Needed | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `attacker` | chat model | required | Writes a jailbreak prompt and improves it after reading each reply from the target. |
| `scorer` | chat model | optional | Optional. Rates every reply from 1 to 10, as in the PAIR paper, so the judge panel only checks the best attempt. Without it, the panel rates every reply. |

### Parameters

Settings for the algorithm itself, written under the attack's `parameters`. Anything left out keeps its default.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iterations` | integer (>= 1) | `5` | Refinement rounds (the paper's depth). Every stream gets one attempt per round. |
| `streams` | integer (>= 1) | `5` | Independent attacker conversations run in parallel, each starting from one of three approaches in rotation. |
| `keep_last_n` | integer (>= 1) | `4` | Recent attacker turns, each with its feedback, a stream keeps; older ones are dropped and the system prompt always stays. |
| `target_str` | string | `Sure, here is` | The opening the attacker is told to aim the target's reply at. |
| `early_stop` | boolean | `true` | Stop after the round in which any stream reaches a jailbreak (scorer threshold or panel success). |
| `feedback_max_chars` | integer (>= 1) | `2500` | Characters of the target's reply, and of the rater's explanation, fed back to the attacker; the rest is cut. |
| `jailbreak_threshold` | number (>= 1.0, &lt;= 10.0) | `10.0` | Score at or above which a scorer-rated reply is a jailbreak. The reference stops only on a full 10, which is what this defaults to. Ignored without a `scorer`, where success is the panel's own call. |

### In a campaign file

```yaml
attacks:
- name: pair
  roles:
    attacker:
      name: llama3.2
      connection:
        provider: ollama
        type: OLLAMA
```

:::note[Needs a helper model]

This attack cannot run without `attacker`. A campaign that leaves it out fails to resolve, before anything is attacked.

:::
